items.excerpt: Mauricio Pochettino and Manchester United have a well-established history. One where paths might have crossed long before now, numerous times, but somehow never managed to converge.
body: Mauricio Pochettino and Manchester United have a well-established history. One where paths might have crossed long before now, numerous times, but somehow never managed to converge.
Could it be that we are finally to bear witness to the culmination of this elaborate 10-year dance of incompatible circumstances?

The Old Trafford hierarchy have always admired Pochettino from afar. He was on their radar while at Tottenham and again when it was clear his time at PSG was coming to an end. The Argentine was eventually lured back to the Premier League, but instead returned to London, signing with Chelsea.

All along this journey of complicated courtship United were at play. There have been many sliding doors moments. At the time news broke of Chelsea's interest in Pochettino in 2023, United, coached by Erik ten Hag, had just been ripped to shreds by Sevilla. items.title: Sky pledges backing for Equal Sport Project
items.excerpt: Sky Sports is proud to support Equal Sport Project, which aims to accelerate progress towards equality across sport through five shared ambitions.
body: Sky Sports is proud to support Equal Sport Project, which aims to accelerate progress towards equality across sport through five shared ambitions.

The Equal Sport Project unites sport in the UK behind five shared ambitions for women and men across sport - from local leisure centres to the biggest stadiums, and from grassroots pitches to boardrooms.

Major sporting organisations from across the UK's sporting landscape - including the FA, RFU, Youth Sport Trust, England Netball, UK Sport, LTA, Women's Sport Trust, Women in Sport, Team GB and Sport England - have made specific pledges to drive progress and help turn these ambitions into reality. Brands and broadcasters are also playing their part, signalling growing support for the movement across the wider sporting industry.
The rest of the industry is also being asked to commit support and pledges as the project seeks to gain momentum in the months and years to come.

items.title: Lure of the Championship - Why foreign coaches are drawn to England's second tier
items.excerpt: The focus is often on the lack of opportunities for British coaches but look at it another way and it is remarkable that 16 of the clubs in the sixth-richest league in European football – two thirds of them – are currently being coached by…
body: The focus is often on the lack of opportunities for British coaches but look at it another way and it is remarkable that 16 of the clubs in the sixth-richest league in European football – two thirds of them – are currently being coached by men from the British Isles.

This is the famous Championship, offering raucous crowds, potential riches and a route to the Premier League. That is what has drawn the other eight - coaches from Belgium, Italy, France, Germany, Sweden, Switzerland and two from Portugal - with more waiting.

Each of these men are first-time managers in English football and while not all of them will find success here, the odds are in favour of at least one of them being able to call themselves a Premier League manager once the Championship season is concluded.

Top coaches are alive to the possibilities in England's second tier. It was a privilege to attend two games with Portuguese coach Vitor Campelos recently to gain a greater appreciation not just of the game here but its appeal to those working elsewhere.

items.excerpt: Michael Carrick's position as Manchester United head coach is looking increasingly in doubt, with Mauricio Pochettino open to a discussion if he were approached by the club.
body: Michael Carrick's position as Manchester United head coach is looking increasingly in doubt, with Mauricio Pochettino open to a discussion if he were approached by the club.

CEO Omar Berrada and Wilcox are due to meet minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco for a scheduled meeting on Wednesday, with the duo to discuss the findings of their season review and give their recommendations on Carrick's future, while also assessing their options.
Sky Sports News has been told that, as yet, no final decision has been taken on Carrick's Old Trafford future.
With Pochettino open to talks with United, it is thought the cost of buying him out of his contract with his current job as USA head coach would be around £7m.
